newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian govt close to 1997 budget deal - PM office.
newsitem.headline: Belgian govt close to 1997 budget deal - PM office.

text.p: The Belgian government is close to a deal on the 1997 budget, Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene's spokeswoman said on Thursday.
"We are getting close to the finishing line. It is now just a matter of finding agreement on the last few billions," Moniek Delvou told Reuters.
Analysts estimate the total 1997 austerity package will be worth around 100 to 110 billion francs.
Dehaene is due to present his budget in parliament on Tuesday, October 1 at 1500 local (1300 GMT).
Delvou said the government would stick to its target of cutting the 1997 deficit to less than three percent of gross domestic product (GDP). She did not specify how much below three percent.
She said the atmosphere in the budget negotiations was "good". Key ministers were expected to work through the weekend to finalise the budget text.
"Work will continue until Monday night," she said.
She declined to elaborate on specific measures.
Belgian media said they expected one third spending cuts, one third new taxes and one third non-fiscal measures such as further privatisations and other one-shot measures.

On the taxation side, there have been reports of higher excise duties on beer and spirits and a two-franc per litre increase in the tax on petrol. The government is also considering a "turnover tax" on regulated savings accounts.
On the spending cuts side, the main measure is the planned rise in the women's retirement age to 65 from the current 60. This would be done gradually over a period of 10 years or more.
Among the one-off measures are a possible further privatisation of ASLK-CGER bank.

Belgian television RTBF said there was already agreement on 42 billion francs worth of measures in the social security sector, 32 billion in fiscal receipts and 10 billion in the various government departments.
Belgian unions staged protest actions in Brussels today in which about 1,500 people took part.
Belgian Finance Minister Philippe Maystadt told union members at a demonstration at his house before sunrise today that they "should not fear for a social massacre".
